lead: Every Boolean function takes n bits to one bit, and every such function can be written as a Boolean polynomial: a formula built only from variables, AND, OR and NOT. The two standard forms are canonical DNF, an OR of minterms, and canonical CNF, an AND of maxterms. These forms turn a truth table into an equation. Circuit designers use them to build adders and comparators, and examiners use them to test whether you can move between a table and a formula. Only a few universities treat Boolean functions as a separate chapter.
prereq: You need: normal forms from Unit 1 and Boolean algebra laws from Chapter 5.5.

blocks.text: A Boolean function of n variables is a map f:{0,1}^n→{0,1}. It takes an n-bit input and returns one bit. For n=2 the inputs are 00, 01, 10, 11. A Boolean polynomial is an expression in variables using OR (∨), AND (∧) and NOT (′). Example: x′y+xy′. The expression is not unique; the canonical forms give one standard choice.

A literal is a variable or its complement. A minterm is an AND of n literals, one for each variable, either xi or xi′. For x,y the minterms are x′y′, x′y, xy′, xy. A maxterm is an OR of n literals, one for each variable. For x,y the maxterms are x+y, x+y′, x′+y, x′+y′.

blocks.where: f is the Boolean function; a_i is the i-th input bit string in the table; m_i is the minterm true only at a_i; M_i is the maxterm false only at a_i.

blocks.text: Canonical DNF is the OR of the minterms for which f=1. Canonical CNF is the AND of the maxterms for which f=0. Every Boolean function has both forms. For n variables there are 2^n minterms and 2^n maxterms. Some syllabi call DNF sum of products and CNF product of sums.

items: List all 2^n input rows and compute f for each row.
For each row with f=1, write its minterm.
OR those minterms: this is the canonical DNF.
For each row with f=0, write its maxterm.
AND those maxterms: this is the canonical CNF.

blocks.text: A minterm is 1 only on its own row. A maxterm is 0 only on its own row. So the OR of selected minterms copies the 1 rows, and the AND of selected maxterms copies the 0 rows. Do not mix: maxterms never go in a DNF, and a minterm must contain every variable.

figure.caption: The truth table marks the two minterms where XOR is 1 and the two maxterms where it is 0; the two 1 rows build the DNF and the two 0 rows build the CNF.

spec.title: XOR: f = x′y + xy′
spec.aria: Truth table for XOR on two variables, listing the minterms m1 and m2 where f is 1 and the maxterms M0 and M3 where f is 0.

examples.question: For f(x,y)=x′y+xy′, write the canonical DNF and canonical CNF, and evaluate both at inputs 10 and 11.
steps: f=1 at 01 and 10. Minterms: m1=x′y, m2=xy′.
f=0 at 00 and 11. Maxterms: M0=x+y, M3=x′+y′.
examples.answer: The canonical DNF is x′y+xy′, the canonical CNF is (x+y)(x′+y′); at input 10 both give 1, and at input 11 both give 0.

traps: Using maxterms in a DNF or minterms in a CNF. DNF uses minterms where f=1; CNF uses maxterms where f=0.
Leaving a variable out of a minterm or maxterm. Canonical forms use every variable exactly once in every term.
Reading a 0 bit as a complemented literal in a maxterm. In a maxterm, bit 0 gives the uncomplemented variable and bit 1 gives the complemented variable.
Confusing canonical DNF with a simplified DNF. xy′+x′y is canonical for XOR; adding x′y′ is wrong because it makes f=1 at 00.

quiz.q: Define minterm and maxterm for n Boolean variables.
quiz.a: Minterm: AND of n literals, one per variable, true on one row. Maxterm: OR of n literals, one per variable, false on one row.

quiz.q: Why does canonical DNF use only rows with f=1?
quiz.a: Each minterm is 1 on exactly one row, so the OR of those rows gives 1 exactly where f=1.

quiz.q: For f(x,y)=x∧y, write canonical DNF and CNF.
For f(x,y)=x∨y, write canonical DNF and CNF.
A student writes XOR as x′y+xy′+x′y′. What is wrong and what is correct?
quiz.a: The extra minterm x′y′ makes f=1 at 00. Correct DNF is x′y+xy′.

quiz.q: Why do canonical DNF and CNF of the same function look different but agree?
quiz.a: DNF lists 1 rows; CNF lists 0 rows. Both reproduce the same truth table, so they are equal as functions.

beyond: Not for the exam. Boolean polynomials also appear as algebraic normal forms over GF(2), used in coding theory and cryptography. Circuit synthesis tools convert truth tables into two-level AND-OR or OR-AND forms. SAT solvers and binary decision diagrams manipulate Boolean functions far larger than a hand truth table. Search next for algebraic normal form, Reed–Muller expansion, and binary decision diagram.
